author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Slip, This Dow Jones Stock Takes A Dive | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks slipped from mixed trade to tight losses Friday as early comments from a key Trump administration official stirred some optimism, and the Dow Jones industrial average struggled to defend its narrow gain for the month.
X
A handful of tech leaders rose early on earnings news, led by Ambarella ( AMBA ), Workday ( WDAY ) and VMWare ( VMW ). On the downside, Goldman Sachs ( GS ) slumped after an analyst downgrade followed reports that the Federal Reserve ramped up a probe into the company's internal controls. Chipmaker Cree ( CREE ) fell on an analyst downgrade. Marriott International ( MAR ) tumbled after reporting a breach of its Starwood guest reservation system compromising data of as many as 500 million consumers .
The Dow Jones industrial average opened down 0.2% as Goldman Sachs weighed heavy on early trade. The S&P 500 traded down less than 0.1%. The Nasdaq Composite edged briefly higher, then slipped 0.1%.
FANG stocks traded lower in early action, and Apple ( AAPL ) slipped 0.5%. Workday notched the strongest gain among Nasdaq 100 stocks. Marriott fell 5%, to the bottom of the Nasdaq 100. Laboratory Corp. of America ( LH ) posted the S&P 500's worst decline.
Lighthizer Expects Success The market took a breather Thursday, after Wednesday's rousing follow-through session . But concerns regarding the general gathering of G20 leaders in Argentina — and specifically over the trade chat planned Saturday between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping — have kept a lid on further gains.
News reports Friday said U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer expected the Trump/Xi meeting to be a success .
For November, the stock market's three leading indexes are in somewhat different situations. The Dow Jones industrial average is up 0.9% through Thursday and working on its fourth gain in the past five months. The S&P 500 is ahead 1%, leaning toward its seventh advance in eight months. The Nasdaq had slipped 0.5% for the month through Thursday, in what would mark its third straight monthly decline.
The Nasdaq has, however, fought hardest over the past week. The index gained 4.8% through Thursday, rising to within 2% of its 50-day moving average. The S&P 500 advanced 4% so far this week, ending Thursday's session less than 1% below its converged 50- and 200-day lines.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 4.3%. That placed it back above its 200-day moving average, as well as the 25,000 mark, and within 1% of its 50-day line.
Goldman Sachs, Sprouts Slip; Workday Eyes Buy Point Dow Jones stock Goldman Sachs dropped more than 2%. Bank of America downgraded the stock from buy to neutral, and carved its price target to 225, from 280. The report cited uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's investigation.
Bloomberg reported late Thursday that the Federal Reserve had ramped up its probe into company compliance failures . A former company official pleaded guilty earlier this month to laundering money, violating the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and conspiring to conceal facts from Goldman's compliance and legal staff. In a statement to the court, the former official said his behavior was "very much in line of its culture of Goldman Sachs to conceal facts from certain compliance and legal employees," according to Bloomberg. Goldman stock was up 3% for the week through Thursday, seeking to reverse a sharp three-week sell-off.
Workday spiked nearly 8% in early trading. The enterprise software maker reported late Thursday revenue, profit and billings that topped analyst expectations . The stock briefly cleared a potential buy point at 157.22 in a two-month base pattern .
Among IBD 50 stocks, Atlassian ( TEAM ) jumped almost 3% to an early lead. The stock is climbing the right side of a possible two-month base pattern.
Sprouts Farmers Market ( SFM ) dropped nearly 15%. The natural foods grocer announced late Thursday that Chief Executive Amin Maredia would exit the company at the end of the year. COO Jim Nielsen and CFO Brad Lukow will cover CEO duties while the company seeks a replacement.
Stock Futures: Amabrella Jumps, Cree Dives Chipmaker Ambarella roared almost 13% higher after a 75% earnings slip and a 36% revenue decline were not as bad as analysts expected. The big-volume move sent the stock back above its 10-week moving average, but left it still deep in a 10-month consolidation.
Cree tanked more than 5%, after JPMorgan downgraded the stock to underweight, from neutral. The note cited valuation, and held the stock's price target at 35. Cree shares are still up 30% since mid-October, climbing the right side of a three-month up base.
China's Hang Seng: Strongest Month Since January Stocks in China recovered from early losses Friday but trade remained weak as investors awaited news from the Trump-Xi G20 meeting. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index edged up 0.2%, giving it a 2.2% gain for the week and a 6.1% gain for November. The Hang Seng's first monthly advance in seven months left the index well above its 10-week moving average, as it attempts to form a bottom in its pullback into bear market territory.
The Shanghai Composite climbed 0.8%, Friday. That left it down 0.3% for the week, with a 0.5% loss for November and still unable to crack resistance at its 10-week line.
Europe's markets traded lower Friday. London's FTSE 100 remained down 0.6% in afternoon trade. Frankfurt's DAX was off 0.5% and the CAC-40 in Paris traded down 0.2%. All three indexes were tracking toward narrow gains for the week, and toward modest losses for November.
